summary: Focus on the actions within your control without becoming consumed by the outcome.
Pleasure and pain are temporary experiences that come and go.
The true self is eternal and is not destroyed when the body dies.
A steady person remains balanced through suffering, fear, attachment, and anger.
Repeated fixation creates attachment, which can grow into unhealthy desire.
Uncontrolled anger clouds judgment and can lead to destructive decisions.
Perform your responsibilities sincerely without becoming attached to rewards.
True knowledge gradually brings clarity and inner purification.
The mind can become either your greatest supporter or your greatest obstacle.
Whenever the mind wanders, gently bring it back under your awareness.
The restless mind can gradually be controlled through consistent practice and detachment.
Inner steadiness allows a person to remain free from excessive fear, anxiety, and agitation.
When the burden feels too heavy, surrendering excessive fear and seeking a higher refuge can bring peace.
